objective: Restore privacy-valid persisted conversations across SPA navigation and refresh, retain inspectable new-turn provenance and speech, avoid stale cache or cancelled-draft resurrection

cacheExperiment.method: Actual ChatPage with controlled fetch/SSE and a real QueryClient; inspect mutation cache after unmount and a next task

readApi.authentication: existing token requirement, read only, no model or tool replay
readApi.pagination: positive before_id optional, limit 1..200 default100; older rows available explicitly; stable source IDs and same revision required across pages
readApi.snapshot: instance_id, revision, items ordered by source id, has_more, next_before_id
readApi.item: id, role user/assistant, text, session_id, created_at, redacted, optional original ChatResult for valid stored new assistant trace
readApi.redaction: Join current message contents; never replay old plaintext traces across a privacy revision. Old records without stored trace remain readable with honest provenance availability.

requiredScenarios: legacy messages readable without fabricated trace
new completed turns restore exact role/text/source IDs and original trace
SPA navigation restores conversation, including older pages
history read and replay UI do not call models or tools
cancel before final commit does not restore an assistant draft
read during a pending turn does not duplicate its user row
forget source and dependent replies clears old traces in the same revision transaction
held old history response cannot override a newer privacy event/snapshot
held old final result cannot repopulate rows after privacy clear
cross-tab privacy notification and focus refresh revalidate without localStorage transcript
original playback and cancellation tests remain valid
finite long-history browser run and resource observations with explicit duration
gates: Exact content/source/trace checks, no cancelled assistant restore, no erased marker in current UI or returned trace, no duplicate rows or model/tool re-execution from reads, all required regressions pass
limitations: Finite fixtures and HTTP/SSE tests do not approve general semantics, human ASR/vowels, physical AV or multi-day stability. Cache entry counts do not alone explain all heap growth.
